newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on exporters activity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on exporters activity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart on Saturday as exporters emerged sold U.S. dollars, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.727 against Friday's T$27.735 close. Turnover through dealers was a slow US$45 million.
The Taiwan dollar decline was partly due to weakness of the U.S. dollar overseas, dealers said.
"It's a quiet day with thin turnover, so exporter's U.S. dollar selling easily pushed up the Taiwan dollar," said one dealer.
Dealers said fund outflows had slowed as foreign funds' profit-taking on stocks triggered by political fears had eased.
Jitters over unsettled domestic politics are easing after President Lee Teng-hui promised at a news conference on Thursday that Premier Lien Chan will step down in July, dealers said.
"Foreign fund outflows had eased, and we even saw some equity fund inflows on Friday," the dealer said.
For next week, a T$27.68-27.78 range was seen.
